title: Bath-state (In)dependence of Non-Markovianity Measures in Quadratic Open Systems
authors: Mirko Consiglio, Ilia Khomchenko, Tony J. G. Apollaro
abstract: Open quantum system dynamics fail to fulfill the conditions of the Markov approximation when the environment and system timescales are close to each other. Such behavior of these systems can be characterized by several non-Markovianity measures, which are expected to vary with the environment parameters. In this work, we consider a fermionic quadratic open quantum system, establishing bath-state independence of the Breuer--Laine--Piilo and the Lorenzo--Plastina--Paternostro non-Markovianity measures. However, our analytical results reveal that the entanglement-based and divisibility-based Rivas--Huelga--Plenio measures, as well as the entropic Megier--Smirne--Vacchini measure, remain sensitive to the reservoir state, through both its temperature and its chemical potential. Modeling the reservoir as a free-fermionic chain, we derive an exact time-local master equation for a single fermionic site in contact with it. Our numerical results for this model confirm these findings and show that the BLP and LPP measures vanish identically only on the bound-state threshold, where the bath-sensitive measures nevertheless remain finite.
summary: This paper analyzes non-Markovianity in a fermionic quadratic open quantum system to determine which diagnostic measures are robust against changes in the environment's state. It proves that two measures (BLP and LPP) are bath-state independent, while others are sensitive to the bath's temperature and chemical potential. This helps theorists select appropriate metrics for characterizing memory effects in complex quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the dependence of various non-Markovianity measures on the specific state of the environment (bath) in open quantum systems.
main_result: For a fermionic quadratic open system, the BLP and LPP non-Markovianity measures are proven to be independent of the bath state, while other measures (like RHP and MSV) remain sensitive to the bath's temperature and chemical potential.
method: The analysis involves deriving time-local master equations for the system dynamics and applying theoretical tools to calculate and compare multiple non-Markovianity measures.
model_or_system: The model is a fermionic quadratic open quantum system consisting of a single fermionic site coupled to a reservoir of multiple sites. The dynamics are governed by a quadratic Hamiltonian, allowing for exact time-local master equation derivations.
key_observables: Non-Markovianity measures: Breuer–Laine–Piilo (BLP), Lorenzo–Plastina–Paternostro (LPP), Rivas–Huelga–Plenio (RHP), and Megier–Smirne–Vacchini (MSV).
important_parameters: Bath temperature ($ eta$) and chemical potential ($\mu$); the system is analyzed in the context of quadratic Hamiltonians.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the bath state being parity-even and the system Hamiltonian being quadratic. The analysis is restricted to these specific mathematical structures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the quadratic system–bath model, detailing the coupling terms between the single fermionic site and the reservoir.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model, derives the time evolution equations leading to a time-local master equation, and then systematically analyzes and compares the mathematical dependence of five different non-Markovianity measures on the bath state.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial theoretical insight into the robustness of different non-Markovianity diagnostics, distinguishing which measures are fundamentally robust (bath-independent) versus those that are highly sensitive to environmental details.
